strongest_supported_claim.overall: The combined package is defensibly ready for an internal report as a bounded effectiveness deliverable. Within that package, task003 can be retained as a narrow patent-candidate lead, while task004 remains internal-report-ready only. Neither task is ready for a paper-candidate claim.
strongest_supported_claim.task003: Under a single representative condition, inverter reactive-support work has enough bounded task-fit and deliverable support to justify internal reporting and a narrow method-line patent-candidate route, but not a general or paper-grade effectiveness claim.
strongest_supported_claim.task004: Within the current scan envelope, the work supports an internal-report-ready static boundary/screening interpretation for hosting-capacity assessment, but not patent-candidate or paper-candidate positioning.

strongest_unsupported_claim.overall: The current materials support a paper-grade conclusion, a broadly transferable engineering solution, or a stronger unified external effectiveness claim across task003 and task004.
why_unsupported: Task003 is still limited by single-scenario validation, lack of a stronger coordinated comparator, and missing engineering cost / implementability validation.
Task004 is still limited by a narrow scan envelope, missing multi-scenario hosting-capacity evidence, and lack of engineering-standard threshold validation.
The package does not establish that observed gains generalize beyond current scenarios, controls, and validation coverage.

alternative_interpretation: A stricter interpretation would downgrade task003 to internal_report_ready only, treating its current patent_candidate label as an early lead-management tag rather than a deliverable ceiling. That reading is cautious and partly justified by missing novelty/engineering evidence, but it is stricter than the explicit task003 deliverable and claim-routing artifacts currently support.

evidence: A stronger shunt + inverter coordinated comparator
Clearer novelty-separation evidence against nearby technical routes
discriminating_missing_evidence.impact: This evidence would decide whether task003 remains only a bounded patent lead or can move toward stronger patent support or paper-candidate readiness.

evidence: Expanded scan envelope that reaches meaningful boundary-triggering conditions
Voltage-threshold justification aligned to engineering-standard practice
A stronger external benchmark or control-strategy comparator
discriminating_missing_evidence.impact: This evidence would decide whether task004 can move beyond internal framework/report value toward patent-candidate or paper-candidate readiness.

details: Agree that task004 should remain at internal_report_ready.
Agree that neither task should be elevated to paper_candidate.
Agree with the counter that task003's patent ceiling must be interpreted narrowly and not as a broad external-ready claim.
Disagree with fully downgrading task003 to internal_report_ready only, because the reviewed deliverable_package and claim_routing artifacts explicitly support a bounded patent_candidate route.

new_insights: The main adjudication difference is not whether there is any positive signal, but how much deliverable weight task003's current bounded method signal can carry.

The safest package-level recommendation is lower than the strongest single-task route: overall delivery should be internal report, with task003 separated as a patent-candidate lead rather than merged into a stronger package claim.

Task003 and task004 fail upward promotion for different reasons: task003 is bottlenecked by generalization and implementability/novelty separation, while task004 is bottlenecked by boundary realism and standards alignment.
overclaim_warnings: Do not present the combined package as a paper candidate.
Do not treat task003's patent_candidate route as proof of a broadly validated or engineering-ready control solution.
Do not claim task003 establishes a general renewable Volt/Var or full coordinated-control method.
Do not claim task004 reveals the true, unique, or planning-grade hosting-capacity limit of the system.
Do not fuse task003 and task004 into a single stronger effectiveness narrative than their separate evidence supports.

recommended_action.secondary: Retain task003 as a bounded patent-candidate lead inside the report, not as the package-level route.
next_steps: For task003, add multi-scenario validation and a stronger shunt + inverter coordinated comparator.
For task003, add engineering feasibility / cost evidence and clearer novelty separation before any stronger external route.
For task004, expand the scan envelope and add multi-scenario hosting-capacity validation.
For task004, justify thresholds against engineering-standard practice and add a stronger benchmark before any route upgrade.

accepted_interpretation: Accept the interpretation that the package as a whole is ready only for an internal report, while task003 may be preserved as a narrow patent-candidate clue because its own reviewed deliverable and claim-routing artifacts permit that bounded ceiling. Task004 remains internal-report-ready only.
rejected_interpretation: Reject both extremes: reject the optimistic reading that the package is paper-ready or broadly externally ready, and reject the fully conservative reading that task003 has no justified patent-candidate status at all under the current repository routing artifacts.
claim_ceiling_recommendation: At the package level, claim only: 'the current evidence supports an internal report on bounded effectiveness findings; task003 provides a narrow patent-candidate method lead under a single representative condition, and task004 provides an internal-report-ready static boundary/screening result under the current scan envelope.' Do not claim paper-level generalization, engineering-grade completeness, or broad external effectiveness.
